subject: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — latency & throughput recap
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@fastshop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Jamie — great context on FastShop's checkout fraud-eval and the expected traffic patterns. Short recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before the pilot: 

Key customer signals from call:
- Peak checkout QPS: ~420 QPS (estimated peak 30-min window), average ~75 QPS
- P95 latency requirement for checkout path: <= 120ms for tokens generated (end-to-end target)
- Burst characteristic: predictable daily peak with occasional marketing-driven spikes (~2-3x for short windows)
- Data sensitivity: non-PII in prompts; they want audit logs retained for 30 days (ok for Hosted)

Initial qualification: given the combination of high peak QPS and tight P95 requirement, two paths look feasible: 
1) Hosted API with aggressive autoscaling + prefix caching and optimized batching — good for faster time-to-value; we'll need to validate that tail latency meets 120ms under your peak mix.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — more predictable tail latency and better headroom for sustained peak QPS, recommended if we can't meet P95 with hosted during the benchmark.

Proposed next steps:
- You: share (anonymized) QPS/arrival traces for a 72-hour window OR a simple CSV of per-minute QPS for the last week (helps us shape the benchmark).
- Redwood: run a 48-hour hosted benchmark that mirrors your peak-profile (we'll instrument P50/P95/P99 and token cost). If hosted fails P95 at 120ms, we'll run a dedicated pilot sizing pass and provide a TCO comparison.
- Logistics: propose pilot window next Tue–Thu (Oct 26–28). We can provision test keys and a temporary dedicated pod if needed.

Attachments: I attached a starter pilot config (redwood_pilot_config.xlsx) and an SLA draft (rdw_sla_draft.pdf) for your legal and ops teams to review.

If that plan looks right, I'll loop in Alex (infra) to scope the dedicated sizing run and Marissa for pricing/contract.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Park <jamie@fastshop.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Singh <anya@fastshop.com>, FastShop DevOps Team <ops@fastshop.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Thanks, Rishi — that recap is spot on. Couple clarifications from our side: 
- We'll export the last 7 days of per-minute checkout QPS and strip any user IDs — ops can drop that into the CSV. Expect that by Wed EOD (Oct 21).
- The 120ms P95 is the downstream SLA (total system) — for the model call specifically, we can tolerate up to ~70ms P95 if our application layer is ~40–50ms. That gives you more room for hosted to qualify.
- Regarding spikes: marketing team runs flash discounts that can spike to ~950 QPS for 3–7 minutes; those are rare (~8–10x per quarter) but we want graceful degradation rather than errors.

We're ok with the proposed Oct 26–28 window for the hosted benchmark. We'll need a basic scope of what telemetry you need from our side (metrics/traces/endpoints).

– Jamie
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@fastshop.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the P95 breakdown — that helps. Alex, can you review the telemetry asks below and confirm we can run the hosted benchmark with the customer's input?

Telemetry/inputs we'll need from FastShop:
- Per-minute QPS CSV for last 7 days (ops said Wed EOD).
- Representative sample prompts (anonymized) and average token lengths for the checkout path.
- Any rate-limiting rules or client-side timeouts we should emulate.

What Redwood will supply for the benchmark:
- Hosted benchmark harness (streaming and non-streaming modes), instrumented to report P50/P95/P99 latency at token-level and end-to-end simulated-app latency.
- A simulated client that can replay your arrival trace and inject marketing spike windows at 10x to test graceful degradation.
- If hosted cannot meet the 70ms model-level P95 target during peak, we'll propose a dedicated pod sizing (GPU type + instance count) and an estimated monthly reserved cost plus delta to hosted for the workload.

Marissa/Ben — once benchmark completes we'll need a pricing approval and a draft contract addendum for short-term reserved capacity (if needed).

I'll set the pilot window on our side and send an invite for Oct 26 09:00 PT to kick off.

Rishi
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — infra ask and tentative sizing

Quick infra note after skimming the CSV template in the attachment: if their peaks are sustained above ~600 QPS for more than 10–15 minutes, hosted will likely need aggressive autoscaling with multiple warm nodes; that increases token-cost delta vs dedicated but may still meet P95 if we tune batching and KV prefix caching. For the Oct 26 trial I'll prepare two runs: 
- Run A: Hosted baseline with their trace + default caching/batching profiles.
- Run B: Hosted tuned (max concurrent handlers, smaller batch windows for tail latency) to attempt hitting 70ms model P95.
- If both fail, I'll propose a Dedicated configuration: 4 x A100-style pods (quantized model path) as a starting point — costs and expected P95 in the report.

I'll attach a short infra checklist to the pilot invite.

— Alex
From: Jamie Park <jamie@fastshop.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Singh <anya@fastshop.com>, FastShop DevOps Team <ops@fastshop.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification: hosted vs dedicated — follow-up and next steps

Perfect — ops attached the per-minute CSV to the HubSpot record and we've shared sample prompts in the Drive link you provided. We're good to kick off Oct 26. A few asks before the run: 
- Can Redwood include a short run that simulates an 8-minute flash spike at 950 QPS so we can see failover behavior?
- We'll want the pilot report to explicitly call out expected unit-cost (per 1k tokens) for hosted vs the proposed dedicated configuration so procurement can review quickly.

If those are in scope, proceed with the invites and we'll confirm the internal stakeholders for the post-run readout.

Thanks — Jamie
